text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock fell slightly today as oil prices gained but refiners faced headwinds from rising crude costs and uncertainty. US oil rose to $107 a barrel, but the bigger story is geopolitical noise—Iran signaled willingness to reopen the Strait of Hormuz with conditions, and Ukraine floated an "energy ceasefire" with Russia. These diplomatic hints suggest the market is pricing in potential supply relief, which would hurt refiner margins. Meanwhile, refineries are running at 96.8% capacity, and storage levels remain elevated, leaving little room for refinery operators to pass higher input costs to customers.

The stock's three-day slide from $425 to $387 reflects a broader shakeout in energy—Wall Street itself admitted it has no idea where oil is headed amid the Iran situation. Without clear direction on geopolitics or crude supply, refiners like Marathon face margin compression from their main input cost swinging wildly while demand-side dynamics stay murky.
